2.text: Though not obvious to us, the bird--literally, "sparrow"--and swallow--have an object in their motions, so penal evil falls on none without a reason.

3.text: The rod is as much needed by fools and as well suited to them, as whips and bridles are for beasts.

4.text: Answer not--that is, approvingly by like folly.

6.text: A fool fails by folly as surely as if he were maimed. drinketh damage--that is, gets it abundantly (Job 15:16; Job 34:7).

7.text: legs . . . equal--or, "take away the legs," or "the legs . . . are weak." In any case the idea is that they are the occasion of an awkwardness, such as the fool shows in using a parable or proverb (see Introduction; Pro 17:7).

8.text: A stone, bound in a sling, is useless; so honor, conferred on a fool, is thrown away.

9.text: As vexatious and unmanageable as a thorn in a drunkard's hand is a parable to a fool. He will be as apt to misuse is as to use it rightly.

10.text: Various versions of this are proposed (compare Margin). Better perhaps--"Much He injures (or literally, "wounds") all who reward," &c., that is, society is injured by encouraging evil men. transgressors--may be rendered "vagrants." The word "God" is improperly supplied.

11.text: returneth . . . folly--Though disgusting to others, the fool delights in his folly.

12.text: The self-conceited are taught with more difficulty than the stupid.

16.text: The thoughtless being ignorant of their ignorance are conceited.

17.text: meddleth--as in Pro 20:19; Pro 24:21; as either holding a dog by the ears or letting him go involves danger, so success in another man's strife or failure involves a useless risk of reputation, does no good, and may do us harm.

20.text: The talebearers foster (Pro 16:28), and the contentious excite, strife.

23.text: Warm professions can no more give value to insincerity than silver coating to rude earthenware.

24.text: dissembleth--though an unusual sense of the word (compare Margin), is allowable, and better suits the context, which sets forth hypocrisy.

25.text: Sentiment of Pro 26:24 carried out. seven abominations in his heart--that is, very many (compare Pro 24:16).

26.text: Deceit will at last be exposed, and the wicked by their own arts often bring on retribution (compare Pro 12:13; Psa 7:16; Psa 9:17, &c.).

28.text: Men hate those they injure. A lying tongue--"lips" for the persons (compare Pro 4:24; Psa 12:3). Next: Proverbs Chapter 27
